chapters.teaser: The habit everyone's noticed and nobody's mentioned.

chapters.title: Okay fine, the fix (Bom made me)

text.first-impression: Gi, people meet you and want to tell you everything. You're warm, practical, with strong mum-friend energy whatever your age. Ten seconds in, you've offered them water, a snack, or a solution. You notice who's uncomfortable and quietly fix it. What they don't see: you're also worrying. About them, about the plan, about whether you said something weird three minutes ago. Your brain runs a background app called What Could Go Wrong, and it never closes. Not even on holiday. Especially not on holiday. Maybe close a few tabs before bed.
text.your-red-flag: Your red flag: you overgive, then quietly resent it. You'll do the favour, the planning, the emotional heavy lifting, and say it's no trouble at all. Then one day you snap about the dishes and everyone's shocked. It was never about the dishes. It was the last forty things. You also worry so much that you sometimes control. I'm just helping can mean I'm managing you. Let people fail a little. It builds character. Theirs, not yours. Yours is already very well built, thank you. Say the small annoyance when it's still small, before it turns into a dishwasher incident.
text.how-you-sabotage-love: In love you nurture like it's your calling. You cook, remember, plan, comfort. Partners feel cherished, and some of them also get very comfortable and stop doing much at all. Your sabotage is picking people who need a lot of care, because being needed feels safe, and then feeling invisible while you run their life. You deserve someone who notices you're tired before you say it. Also, stop apologising when you ask for things. A request isn't a burden. It's information about how to love you. Write it down if saying it feels too hard.
text.friends-and-work: At work you're the person who knows where everything is and somehow ends up doing three jobs for the price of one. You're dependable, organised, and far too nice about extra tasks. With friends you're the caretaker, the planner, the one who checks in after the hard appointment. But you rarely let anyone check in on you. Being strong for everyone isn't a medal. It's just tiring, and nobody's giving out trophies for it. Let someone else host for once and simply turn up with nothing. Bring nothing. Not even a dessert.
text.the-lie: The lie you tell yourself: it's easier if I just do it. Easier now, much harder later, when you're resentful and exhausted and nobody understands why. You also tell yourself your needs are small. They're not small. They're just quiet. Quiet needs still need meeting, and the people who love you would actually like to meet them, if you'd stop hiding the list. Hand it over. Let them be useful to you for a change. Start small: tell one person one thing you need this week, and then let them actually do it without you supervising.
text.the-fix: The fix, because Bom made a face at me. Say no to one favour a week. Let one person take care of you, and don't repay them within the same hour. Catch yourself apologising and swap sorry for thank you. In love, look for someone who tends your garden too, not just someone who enjoys the view. Close the worry app at night: write it all down, then sleep. You make everyone around you grow. You get to grow too. Write that on a sticky note. Put it on the fridge you clean for everyone.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Gi. You've apologised six times today. For existing.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Gi runs a free care service with no opening hours.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: And 'I'm just helping' sometimes means 'I'm managing you'.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: They do. So let one of them make you dinner. No repaying.

spring.intro: Spring Gi, Wood ran your birth season and Wood controls Earth, so you grew up making room for everyone else's growth. You're the friend who remembers allergies and brings snacks. People see someone nurturing and sweet. Your friends know you'll say yes to helping them move while silently cancelling your own plans. Your red flag is being so busy feeding others that you never ask to be fed. Then you feel invisible and nobody knows why. In love you become their support system and forget to have one. At work you're everybody's helper and nobody's priority. The fix: ask for one favour this week. Someone will be thrilled to help.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You cancelled your own plans to help them move. Again. Fourth move this year.

summer.intro: Summer Gi, Fire ran your season and Fire feeds Earth, so you're warm soil with strong opinions about how the garden should look. Capable, nurturing and a tiny bit bossy. People see the friend who has plasters, snacks and a plan. Your red flag is helpful control. You care, so you advise. You advise, so you assume. In love you might mother your partner a little, and nobody finds that romantic for long. At work you quietly redo other people's tasks. With friends you give advice nobody asked for, lovingly. The fix: ask whether they want advice or want you to listen. Then honour the answer.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You gave unsolicited advice to a stranger at the bus stop. Gi, babe.

autumn.intro: Autumn Gi, Metal ran your birth season and Earth produces Metal, so you're harvest season in human form: productive, generous, always delivering. People see someone incredibly competent. Your friends know you feel guilty resting. Your red flag is measuring your worth in output. If you didn't help, cook or achieve something today, you feel slightly useless. In love you over-function, then wonder why you're tired and unseen. At work you're the safety net for everyone, and safety nets don't get thanked. The fix: one evening a week where you produce nothing. No chores, no favours, no side projects. Lie on the sofa like a vegetable. Try it.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: You're worth love on the days you get nothing done too, Gi.

winter.intro: Winter Gi, Water ran your season and Earth controls Water, so you're soil soaking up everyone's feelings. You're the friend people unload on at parties. People see someone easy to talk to. Your friends see someone who absorbs drama and then can't sleep. Your red flag is emotional sponging. You take on other people's problems as if they're yours, then get muddy and overwhelmed. In love you blur into your partner's mood. At work you carry the office tension home with you. The fix: before you absorb something, ask yourself whose it is. If it isn't yours, care about it without carrying it. Big difference. Practise it.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You absorbed three friends' crises and a colleague's drama this week. Soil, not landfill.

strength.strong: Strong chart, Gi. Rich soil, lots of support, and a firm belief that you know what's best for everyone. You often do. The blind spot: you mother people who didn't ask for a mother. Advice, plans, gentle corrections. It comes from love and lands as control. In love your partner can start to feel like a project. With friends you organise their lives over brunch. The fix: let someone make a choice you think is wrong, and don't comment. Not even a face. Especially not the face. You know the one.
strength.weak: Weak chart, Gi, which means you give from a shallow well and pretend it's bottomless. The blind spot: you're everyone's helper and you feel guilty when you need help yourself. You say it's no trouble when it's a lot of trouble. In love you put their needs first so automatically you forget you have any. At work you're the reliable one who never gets the credit. The fix: let someone do something nice for you without immediately paying it back. Sit with the discomfort. That's the growth.

balance_text.too_much_wood: Too much Wood. You're all growth, plans and ambition, and you never stop reaching. Cute. Also exhausting. You start projects faster than you finish them, and you think rest is for people with fewer goals. You argue to win rather than to understand. Yeon's prescription: prune. Finish one thing before starting another. Say you're right once a week and mean it. A tree that never stops growing eventually just falls over.
balance_text.missing_wood: Missing Wood. Starting things is hard for you, so you just... don't. You wait for the right moment, and the right moment is apparently very busy. You have plans in drafts and ideas in your notes app from three years ago. Yeon's prescription: take the first ugly step today. Send the email. Sign up for the class. Buy the plant. Momentum isn't a mood. It's a decision you make before you feel ready.
balance_text.too_much_fire: Too much Fire. Everything's urgent, everything's dramatic, and your feelings arrive with sirens on. You're fun and bright, and you're also impulsive, and you've sent messages you'd love to unsend. Yeon's prescription: wait one night before any big decision. Drink water, literally and spiritually. Let your calmest friend talk you down before your wildest one hypes you up. Your spark is great. Your house fires are not.
balance_text.missing_fire: Missing Fire. You're lovely, but you're keeping your light on its dimmest setting. You hang back, never celebrate yourself, and assume people won't notice you anyway. That isn't modesty. It's hiding with good manners. Yeon's prescription: be seen. Post the thing, wear the colour, tell the joke out loud. Go outside in the sun. People can't love what they can't see, and you're worth seeing.
balance_text.too_much_earth: Too much Earth. You're stable. Very stable. Possibly too stable. Same restaurant, same route, same opinion, same worry on repeat. You call it reliable. It's also a rut with nice furniture. Yeon's prescription: one new thing a week. It doesn't have to be big. A new food, a new walk, a new person to talk to. Growth needs a little mess, and you can tidy it up afterwards if it makes you feel better.
balance_text.missing_earth: Missing Earth. You're a little all over the place. Plans change, meals get skipped, home is wherever you last dropped your bag. You're adaptable, sure, but you never quite feel settled. Yeon's prescription: routine. Boring, beautiful routine. Same bedtime, real meals, one corner of your home that's only yours. Grounded people make better decisions. Yes, I'm looking directly at you.
balance_text.too_much_metal: Too much Metal. You're sharp, critical, and your opinions come with edges. You decide fast and judge faster. People respect you, and also slightly fear your face in meetings. Yeon's prescription: soften up. Ask before you judge. Let some things stay imperfect. Cry at a film. You can keep your standards and still let people near you without running a full security check first.
balance_text.missing_metal: Missing Metal. Boundaries? Never heard of them. You say yes when you mean no, answer messages at midnight, and lend people your time without ever getting it back. Yeon's prescription: one no a week, with no explanation attached. Declutter something. Unsubscribe, unfollow, unclench. A boundary isn't mean. It's just a door with a lock, and you're allowed to own the key.
balance_text.too_much_water: Too much Water. You think. And think. And then think about what you thought. You feel everything and analyse it until it turns to soup. Your intuition is brilliant. Your sleep schedule is not. Yeon's prescription: get out of your head and into your body. Walk, cook, lift something heavy. Put a timer on the overthinking. Then go and live a little.
balance_text.missing_water: Missing Water. You go, go, go and never stop to feel anything. Rest is for the weak, reflection is a waste of time, and you've been busy for about five years straight. Yeon's prescription: sit still. Ten minutes. No phone. Write one honest line before bed. Your feelings don't disappear because you're running. They just wait for you, patiently, like a bill.

too_much_wood.speaker: yeon
too_much_wood.text: Too much Wood. You started a new life plan on Monday. It's Wednesday. New plan.

too_much_wood.speaker: bom
too_much_wood.text: All that drive is wonderful. Finishing one thing will feel even better.

too_much_fire.speaker: yeon
too_much_fire.text: Too much Fire: three dramatic exits from group chats this year. I counted.

too_much_fire.speaker: bom
too_much_fire.text: Your passion lights rooms up. Count to ten before the big reply.

too_much_earth.speaker: yeon
too_much_earth.text: Heavy Earth: same order, same route, same hoodie since 2019. I see you.

too_much_earth.speaker: bom
too_much_earth.text: Your steadiness makes people feel safe. Try one new thing for fun.

too_much_metal.speaker: yeon
too_much_metal.text: Lots of Metal. Your honesty has made two baristas reconsider their careers.

too_much_metal.speaker: bom
too_much_metal.text: Your clarity is a gift. Wrap it in a little kindness.

too_much_water.speaker: yeon
too_much_water.text: Overflowing Water: you've overthought this reading three times already. Stop.

too_much_water.speaker: bom
too_much_water.text: Your depth is beautiful. Come back to shore when it gets heavy.

missing_wood.speaker: yeon
missing_wood.text: No Wood, no ambition. Your five-year plan is 'see what happens'.

missing_wood.speaker: bom
missing_wood.text: Missing Wood just means growth needs a nudge. One small goal is plenty.

missing_fire.speaker: yeon
missing_fire.text: No Fire. You'd describe your best night out ever as 'fine'. Show some spark!

missing_fire.speaker: bom
missing_fire.text: Missing Fire can mute your joy. Do one thing just because it's fun.

missing_earth.speaker: yeon
missing_earth.text: No Earth. You've changed flat, job and hair colour twice this year.

missing_earth.speaker: bom
missing_earth.text: Missing Earth makes it hard to settle. A simple routine is grounding.

missing_metal.speaker: yeon
missing_metal.text: No Metal. You've never said no to anyone in your life, have you?

missing_metal.speaker: bom
missing_metal.text: Missing Metal means boundaries take practice. Start with one tiny no.

missing_water.speaker: yeon
missing_water.text: No Water. Someone cried in front of you and you offered a snack.

missing_water.speaker: bom
missing_water.text: Missing Water can hide feelings. Name one out loud today.
